purpose: Measure, per crate, where network responsibility actually lives, against the rules RFC-NET-001 and AGENTS.md state. Exists because the previous three weeks produced a ratified specification describing an architecture that was never built, and 33 hardcoded DNS zones, 2 imperative network I/O sites, and 93 files inverting the DAG survived underneath it. This audit is a measurement, not a verdict: it records what is observed so the next tranche order is derived from evidence rather than from intent.

method.loc_count: wc -l over every .rs file in the crate's src/ tree
method.test_exclusion: per-line classification: a line is a fixture when it is inside an inline #[cfg(test)] / #[cfg(any(test, kani))] module, lives in a tests.rs file, or is a comment. Classifying per line rather than per file matters: truncating a file at its first test module discards production code that appears later in the same file.
method.dag_rule: a dependency is an inversion only when the target crate's layer is strictly above the source crate's layer
method.not_a_tool: produced by reading the tree with grep and a Python pass; reproducible by re-running the same greps, but no committed CYNIC surface generates it yet
known_limits: layer assignment is hand-maintained, derived from AGENTS.md; a crate absent from that list defaults to L2, so a misclassified crate produces a false negative or a false positive in the DAG table
the DNS filter is the literal string 'synapse.cynic'; a zone built at runtime from fragments is invisible to it
the imperative-I/O filter matches Command::new("ping|wg|ip|nft|...") per occurrence and records the matched binary; an argv assembled through a variable is invisible to it

rules_under_audit.rule: All network data models, parsing algorithms, route planning, access control rendering and drift evaluations reside in cynic-network, pure. Network I/O occurs strictly behind explicit boundaries in adapters/.

rules_under_audit.source: AGENTS.md Architecture & Crate Invariants, Zero-I/O Domain Core
rules_under_audit.rule: Domain modules are 100% pure: no std::process, no reqwest, no tokio::spawn. Side effects stay behind explicit Ports in runner.rs or adapters/.
cynic-host and cynic-node are monoliths under strict ratchet: no net growth. Autonomous sub-domains must be clean-room extracted.
Higher layers depend on lower layers, never the reverse. Pure domain crates never depend on orchestrator or host crates.
The canonical service DNS zone is service.cynic, owned by cynic-network::dns::DEFAULT_DNS_ZONE. No crate may hardcode it; consumers read the authority.

dns_zone.note: cynic-node::dns_contract::default_dns_zone() is the de facto authority for five call sites inside cynic-node, so removing it requires re-pointing those callers at cynic-network. cynic-network already holds the correct value and nobody imports it.

planes.state: resolved; see RFC-NET-001 §2. Registry files and nine readers are migrated. Remaining legacy surface is field names (synapse_ip / management_ip) and DNS FQDNs.

F-DNS.why_it_matters: the registry declares service.cynic while these sites still emit synapse.cynic, so the DNS bundle a node writes and the names the registry reserves disagree. Two DEFAULT_DNS_ZONE constants exist and neither is the canonical one.
F-DNS.operational_dependency: some sites embed a real server name (forgejo.synapse.cynic, artifacts.synapse.cynic). Renaming the zone in code does not resolve those hosts: every A record and every TLS certificate must move first, or resolution fails at runtime.
F-DNS.blocked_on: operator confirms the DNS cutover order: zone renamed on the hosts, then the code, or a dual-publish window
F-DNS.exclusion_note: 18 production lines across 16 files. 94 further occurrences sit inside inline #[cfg(test)] modules and are excluded: a fixture asserting the pre-migration zone is legitimate while the cutover is in flight. An earlier pass of this audit counted 112 because it truncated each file at its first #[cfg(test)] module and discarded production code written after it; the figure was corrected by classifying each line rather than each file.

sites.why: a projection crate shells out to WireGuard directly; the same read already exists behind cynic_host::wireguard_readback and cynic_network::adapters::host_probe
network keepalive spawned directly from an orchestration crate instead of through cynic_network::adapters::host_probe, which already reads the same L2/L3 state

related_duplication.why: two crates own WireGuard read-back; one parses dump, the other latest-handshakes, neither delegates to the other

F-DAG.correction_to_earlier_claims: RFC-NET-001 §7 named peer_resolver_mesh.rs as the single DAG inversion. Measured, it is 86 files: 82 in cynic-host, 3 in cynic-lifecycle, 1 in cynic-discovery-host. cynic-host is the bulk and the inversion reaches cynic-build, cynic-node-protocol, cynic-storage, cynic-eval, cynic-intel and cynic-inference.
F-DAG.cynic_network_is_clean: cynic-network has zero outbound dependencies above L1. The T1-T5 extraction left the core genuinely pure.

F-RATCHET.network_share: cynic-node carries roughly 11000 LOC across 31 network-named modules. Most of it is projection and convergence, which is legitimate L3 work; only the F-IO and F-DNS sites are violations. The ratchet failure is net growth, not the network domain's presence.
F-RATCHET.note: foundation.json declares the 25k god-object ceiling as a hard boundary. No layer_debt record was found declaring an exception for either crate.

explicit_non_goals: this audit does not judge whether the ~11000 network LOC in cynic-node should exist; projection, convergence and actuation are legitimate L3 responsibilities
it does not propose a target architecture; it orders what the measurements justify
it does not audit the 126 test fixtures that still carry the legacy zone; fixtures are allowed to assert the pre-migration contract while the migration is in flight

proposed_sequence.scope: delete the two duplicate DEFAULT_DNS_ZONE constants and the local fallback; re-point every consumer at cynic_network::dns::DEFAULT_DNS_ZONE; leave the server FQDNs for the cutover that requires the operator
proposed_sequence.blocked_on: operator decision on the DNS cutover order

proposed_sequence.scope: cynic-host's 82 inverted files, plus 4 in cynic-lifecycle and cynic-discovery-host. Not one tranche: it needs a dependency-inversion pass per target crate, starting with cynic-node-protocol because peer_resolver_mesh and local_autonomy_runtime sit on it
watchdog.rs keepalive and cli scan route through cynic-network adapters; collapse the two WireGuard read-backs into one owner
declare layer_debt or split cynic-host below the 25k ceiling; currently the hard boundary is violated silently

verification.reproduce_dag: for c in cynic-host cynic-lifecycle cynic-discovery-host; do grep -rl 'cynic_build::\|cynic_node_protocol::\|cynic_storage::' --include=*.rs crates/$c/src/; done | wc -l
verification.baseline: edbf8fae (the parent of the T4.3 vocabulary tranche) for failure attribution

ratification.promotion_condition: the operator accepts the finding counts and the tranche order; the audit then moves to contracts/ and becomes an enforceable gate
ratification.authority_note: infra/ is not a source of truth. This file is a measurement record, not an authority; contracts/ is where a constraint that may fail a build belongs.
